svg.title: Figure GK-4. Cargo tiedowns (count and strength)
svg.desc: From CA Commercial Driver Handbook DL 650 (REV 12/2019) sections 3.3.1-3.3.3 (blocking, bracing, tiedowns, header boards): at least one tiedown per 10 feet of cargo, and at least two tiedowns no matter how small; aggregate WLL at least 1/2 the cargo weight.

svg.text: Federal rule (also in the handbook): aggregate working load limit of the securement system must be at least one-half the weight of the article (or group).

text.tspan: Tiedowns must be the right type and strength (chains, straps, ropes, and tensioning devices as appropriate) and must be attached correctly (hooks, bolts, rails, rings).
Blocking keeps cargo from sliding; it is shaped to fit and is secured to the deck. Bracing runs from the upper part of the cargo to the floor or walls.
Header boards (headache racks) on flatbeds help protect the cab if cargo shifts forward. They must be in good condition.

There are extra rules for logs, dressed lumber, metal coils, paper rolls, concrete pipe, intermodal containers, vehicles, and other specialized cargo -- look them up before you haul those loads (49 CFR 393 Subpart I).
Inspect tiedowns during the pre-trip and again on the road. Cargo that leans, has loose binders, or has shifted is a failing condition.

svg.text: From CA Commercial Driver Handbook DL 650 (REV 12/2019) sections 3.3.1-3.3.3 (blocking, bracing, tiedowns, header boards): at least one tiedown per 10 feet of cargo, and at least two tiedowns no matter how small; aggregate WLL at least 1/2 the cargo weight.
